question: 68 + 92 − 41 + (37 + 15) × 2 − 88 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 135.

GIVEN

• 68 + 92 − 41 + (37 + 15) × 2 − 88

SOLUTION

• Brackets: (37 + 15) = 52

• Multiply: 52 × 2 = 104

• Now, 68 + 92 − 41 + 104 − 88 = 160 − 41 + 104 − 88 = 119 + 104 − 88 = 223 − 88 = 135.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Add all positives and subtract all negatives separately: positives = 68 + 92 + 104 = 264; negatives = 41 + 88 = 129; 264 − 129 = 135.

NOTE

• Always follow BODMAS: Brackets → Of → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction.

question: 88 + (19 × 1) − 33 + 28 + 44 ÷ 2 − 12 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 112.

GIVEN

• 88 + (19 × 1) − 33 + 28 + 44 ÷ 2 − 12

SOLUTION

• (19 × 1) = 19 and 44 ÷ 2 = 22

• 88 + 19 − 33 + 28 + 22 − 12 = 107 − 33 + 28 + 22 − 12 = 74 + 28 + 22 − 12 = 124 − 12 = 112.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Simplify × and ÷ first (19, 22), then group: positives 88 + 19 + 28 + 22 = 157; negatives 33 + 12 = 45; 157 − 45 = 112.

NOTE

• Division and multiplication rank above addition/subtraction in BODMAS, so resolve them before adding.

question:
The line chart given below shows the total loan amount (in Rs. '00000) disbursed by 5 different banks B1, B2, B3, B4 and B5 in the year 2024.

For these 5 banks, what is the average value (in Rs.) of total loan given by each bank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 9100000.

GIVEN

• Loan (in Rs. '00000): B1 = 90, B2 = 130, B3 = 100, B4 = 75, B5 = 60

SOLUTION

• Sum = 90 + 130 + 100 + 75 + 60 = 455

• Average (in '00000) = 455 ÷ 5 = 91

• Actual value = 91 × 100000 = 9100000.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Average the small numbers first (91), then multiply the unit factor '00000 once at the end — avoids handling large zeros throughout.

NOTE

• '00000 means the plotted figure is in hundred-thousands (lakhs); multiply the read value by 100000 to get rupees.

question:
The line chart given below shows the delay (in minutes) on arrival of a train on 6 consecutive days D1, D2, D3, D4, D5 and D6.

What is the average daily delay (in minutes) on these 6 days?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 30.83.

GIVEN

• Delay (minutes): D1 = 44, D2 = 34, D3 = 37, D4 = 5, D5 = 17, D6 = 48

SOLUTION

• Sum = 44 + 34 + 37 + 5 + 17 + 48 = 185

• Average = 185 ÷ 6 = 30.833… ≈ 30.83.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Pair values to add fast: (44+48) + (34+37) + (5+17) = 92 + 71 + 22 = 185, then ÷ 6 = 30.83.

NOTE

• Average = (sum of observations) ÷ (number of observations); 185/6 leaves remainder 5, giving decimal .83.

question:
The pie chart given below shows the quantity of milk sold by 6 shops. The data is presented in the terms of percent.

Quantity of milk sold by P is 60 litres. What is the total quantity (in litres) of milk sold by Q and T?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 300.

GIVEN

• P = 10% = 60 litres; Q = 20%, T = 30%

SOLUTION

• 10% = 60 litres, so 1% = 6 litres and total (100%) = 600 litres

• Q + T = 20% + 30% = 50% of 600 = 300 litres.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Q + T = 50% and P = 10%, so (Q+T) = 5 × P = 5 × 60 = 300 litres directly, without finding the total.

NOTE

• In a percent pie chart, ratio of quantities equals ratio of percentages, so scale one known slice up proportionally.

question:
The bar graph given below shows the number of laptops sold by the given 5 shops.

Which shop sold the maximum number of laptops?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. D.

GIVEN

• Laptops sold: A = 120, B = 150, C = 110, D = 180, E = 140

SOLUTION

• Compare all values: 120, 150, 110, 180, 140

• Highest = 180, which belongs to shop D.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• On a bar graph, the tallest bar is the maximum — just spot the highest bar (D) without reading every value.

NOTE

• 'Maximum' means the greatest value; scan for the tallest column instead of comparing pairwise.

question:
The bar graph given below shows the number of doctors (H1) and nurses (H2) in the given 5 hospitals.

Number of nurses in hospital P are what percent more than the number of doctors in hospital T?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 300%.

GIVEN

• Nurses in P (H2) = 200; Doctors in T (H1) = 50

SOLUTION

• Difference = 200 − 50 = 150

• Percent more = (150 ÷ 50) × 100 = 300%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• 200 is 4 times 50, i.e. 400% of it, so it is 400% − 100% = 300% more.

NOTE

• Percentage more = ((new − base) ÷ base) × 100; the base is the value after 'than' (doctors in T).

question: A 60-gram mixture has a ratio of zinc to copper of 2:1. If the ratio is to be changed to 1:2, what quantity of copper needs to be added?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 60 gram.

GIVEN

• Mixture = 60 g, zinc : copper = 2 : 1; new ratio required = 1 : 2 (copper added)

SOLUTION

• Zinc = 60 × 2/3 = 40 g, Copper = 60 × 1/3 = 20 g

• Zinc stays 40 g. New ratio 1 : 2 ⇒ copper = 2 × zinc = 2 × 40 = 80 g

• Copper to add = 80 − 20 = 60 gram.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Zinc is fixed at 40 g. Zinc's share falls from 2 parts to 1 part, so total scales to 3 × 40 = 120 g; extra = 120 − 60 = 60 g (all copper).

NOTE

• When one ingredient is unchanged, keep its amount constant and rebuild the total from the new ratio.

question: Which number must be subtracted from 1234 to make it a perfect square?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 9.

GIVEN

• Number = 1234; find the value to subtract to get a perfect square

SOLUTION

• 35² = 1225 and 36² = 1296

• Nearest perfect square below 1234 is 1225

• 1234 − 1225 = 9.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• √1234 ≈ 35.1, so take the floor 35; 35² = 1225 and 1234 − 1225 = 9.

NOTE

• To make a number a perfect square by subtraction, subtract the difference from the largest square not exceeding it (⌊√N⌋²).

question:
The table given below shows the number of employees in 6 departments.

What are the total number of employees in D2, D4 and D5?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 1580.

GIVEN

• D2 = 480, D4 = 500, D5 = 600

SOLUTION

• = 980 + 600 = 1580.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

question:
The table given below shows the number of vehicles of type T1, T2 and T3 in 4 showrooms A, B, C and D.

In which showroom, total number of T1, T2 and T3 vehicles are 500?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. B.

GIVEN

• A = 100+160+220, B = 120+180+200, C = 140+200+140, D = 100+80+140

SOLUTION

• A = 480, B = 500, C = 480, D = 320

• Showroom with total 500 is B.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Target is 500; B's largest values (120, 180, 200) are the biggest triple after A — check B first: 120+180+200 = 500. Match.

NOTE

• For 'which row totals X' questions, add row-wise and stop at the first match instead of computing all rows fully.

question: The difference of squares of two consecutive odd numbers is 88. What is the smaller of the two numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 21.

GIVEN

• Two consecutive odd numbers n and n+2 with (n+2)² − n² = 88

SOLUTION

• (n+2)² − n² = 4n + 4 = 88

• 4n = 84 ⇒ n = 21 (numbers 21 and 23).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Difference of squares of two numbers 2 apart = 2 × (sum of the numbers). So sum = 88/2 = 44; the pair is 21 and 23, smaller = 21.

NOTE

• a² − b² = (a+b)(a−b); here a−b = 2, so (a+b) = 44, giving the numbers directly.

question: Which of the following number is NOT divisible by 9?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 4762.

GIVEN

• Test 4762, 4536, 5382, 5211 for divisibility by 9

SOLUTION

• Digit sums: 4762 → 4+7+6+2 = 19 (not a multiple of 9)

• 4536 → 18, 5382 → 18, 5211 → 9 (all multiples of 9)

• So the number NOT divisible by 9 is 4762.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Add digits; if the sum isn't a multiple of 9, the number isn't either. 4762 → 19 → not divisible.

NOTE

• Divisibility by 9: a number is divisible by 9 iff the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.

question: Which of the following number is divisible by both 9 and 11?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 3366.

GIVEN

• Find a number divisible by both 9 and 11

SOLUTION

• Divisible by 9: digit sum 3+3+6+6 = 18 (yes)

• Divisible by 11: (3+6) − (3+6) = 0 (yes)

• So 3366 is divisible by both 9 and 11.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Divisible by both 9 and 11 means divisible by 99. 3366 = 34 × 99, confirming it.

NOTE

• Divisibility by 11: difference between sums of alternate digits is 0 or a multiple of 11.

question: What is the average of first 25 even natural numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 26.

GIVEN

• First 25 even natural numbers: 2, 4, 6, …, 50

SOLUTION

• Sum = 25 × 26 = 650 (using n(n+1) with n = 25)

• Average = 650 ÷ 25 = 26.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Average of first n even natural numbers = (n + 1). Here n = 25, so average = 26 instantly.

NOTE

• First n even numbers: sum = n(n+1), average = n+1; first n odd numbers: average = n.

question: The average of 15 numbers is 55. Four numbers 25, 12, 15 and 36 were removed. What will be the new average?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 67.

GIVEN

• Average of 15 numbers = 55; numbers removed = 25, 12, 15, 36

SOLUTION

• Total sum = 15 × 55 = 825

• Removed sum = 25 + 12 + 15 + 36 = 88; remaining sum = 825 − 88 = 737

• Remaining count = 15 − 4 = 11; new average = 737 ÷ 11 = 67.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• New average = (825 − 88)/11 = 737/11 = 67 — just track total minus removed over the reduced count.

NOTE

• Average = sum ÷ count; when items are removed, subtract their sum and their count together.

question:
In the given figure, angle ABC = 40 degrees and angle BCA = 65 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle ACD?

(Triangle ABC with vertex A at top; base line B–C–D, where D lies on line BC extended beyond C.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 115.

GIVEN

• ∠ABC = 40°, ∠BCA = 65°; ACD is the exterior angle at C

SOLUTION

• ∠ACD is a straight-line angle with ∠BCA: ∠ACD = 180° − 65° = 115°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Exterior angle = sum of two opposite interior angles = ∠BAC + ∠ABC. ∠BAC = 180 − 40 − 65 = 75; 75 + 40 = 115°.

NOTE

• Exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote (non-adjacent) interior angles.

question:
In the given figure, what is value (in degrees) of Q?

(Arrowhead figure: the three angles on the left are 80°, 140° and 10°, and Q is the angle at the right-hand tip.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 50.

GIVEN

• Arrowhead (dart) shape with angles 80°, 10°, a re-entrant (concave) angle of 140°, and tip angle Q

SOLUTION

• The interior angle at the concave vertex is the reflex angle = 360° − 140° = 220°

• Sum of interior angles of the quadrilateral = 360°: 80 + 10 + Q + 220 = 360

• Q = 360 − 310 = 50°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• For an arrowhead, tip angle = (sum of the two outer angles) − reflex-deficit; here 80 + 10 = 90 and the marked 140 gives Q = 90 − (140 − 100)… simply solve 80 + 10 + Q = 140 ⇒ Q = 50°.

NOTE

• In a concave (dart) quadrilateral, one interior angle is reflex; use full-turn 360° for that vertex when applying the angle-sum property.
